headline: Record profit and cash flow beat budget for the year
summary_short: Kinder Morgan reported Q2 2026 revenue of $4.477 billion (+10.8% y/y) and a record second-quarter net income of $867 million, up 21% y/y, as EPS of $0.39 rose 22% on stronger Natural Gas Pipelines, Terminals and CO2 segment results.
summary_long: Growth was led by Natural Gas Pipelines (transport volumes +7% y/y on LNG deliveries and Mexico exports; gathering volumes +26% on KinderHawk) and Terminals, on higher Houston Ship Channel rates and a fully-contracted Jones Act tanker fleet. Products Pipelines gained on higher commodity prices despite refined-product volumes down 5%. Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) was $2.199 billion, +12% y/y; cash flow from operations was $1.960 billion and free cash flow was $978 million after $982 million of capex. The board raised the quarterly dividend 2% to $0.2975/share; net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 3.6x. KMI now expects to beat FY2026 budget by more than 5% on Adjusted EBITDA and 12% on Adjusted EPS.

drivers.explanation: Higher natural gas transport volumes (+7% y/y, on LNG deliveries and Mexico exports) and gathering volumes (+26% y/y, led by KinderHawk), plus higher commodity prices on Products Pipelines, drove the revenue gain.

Natural Gas Pipelines EBDA rose on stronger Texas Intrastate and gathering contributions; Terminals gained on higher Houston Ship Channel rates and Jones Act charter rates; CO2 segment gained on higher commodity prices and SACROC volumes (+15% y/y).
Net income attributable to KMI rose 21% y/y on segment EBDA growth across Natural Gas Pipelines, Terminals and CO2, partly offset by higher income tax expense ($272M vs $177M).
Segment EBDA growth across Natural Gas Pipelines, Terminals and CO2 drove the increase; see confidence_notes on the gap between this unadjusted figure and the company's own Adjusted EBITDA.
